# dsh-rtk
> Route eligible shell commands through rtk (Rust Token Killer) inside the DeepSeek Harness (`dsh`)
bash executor — compress tool output, save tokens, change nothing else.
中文版
> **Heads-up: a `workspace-write` session keeps the compression but loses the ledger and the backups

.**
> The rewrite works in every mode. Confinement is what bites: dsh allows writes only
> inside th

> `history.db`, `recall.db` and `tee/

` in `~/Library/Application Support/rtk` — outside
> those roots. rtk's writes are refused **silentl

y**, so `rtk gain` stays empty and no
> tee backup is kept. Two ways out: run
> `scripts/allow-rtk-s

## Quick Example
The plugin rewrites commands at the `resolve()` boundary — before anything runs:
| Input (`command`) | Resolved output | Reason |

| `git status` | `rtk git status` | rtk has a rule |
| `ls -la` | `rtk ls -la` | rtk routes `ls` too

— no plugin list involved |
| `tree` | `rtk tree` | new in rtk 1.0 — works with **no plugin release

** |
| `head -5 notes.txt` | `rtk read notes.txt --head-lines 5` | rtk's own non-prefix rewrite, ado

pted verbatim |
| `git status \| grep x` | `rtk git status \| grep x` | rtk rewrites the segments it

knows, leaves the rest |
| `cd /tmp` | `cd /tmp` | rtk declines — **identity** |
| `git status` (rt
k absent) | `git status` | binary missing — **identity fallback** |
Everything else — workdir, timeout, env, exit code, sandbox confinement — is inherited unchanged.
## Requirements

- **Node.js:** >= 20.0.0
- **rtk:** `rtk --version` must exit 0 on PATH (install separately, e.g. `c

argo install rtk`)
- **Minimum rtk for the delegation design:** `0.25.0`, where `rtk rewrite` was in
troduced; everything in this README is verified against **`rtk 1.1.0`**, and CI re-runs that check o
n every push. There is no upper bound — see Versioning note.
## Why
LLM agents burn tokens on verbose tool output (`git log`, `cargo build`, `pytest` trails…). `rtk` al
ready knows how to shrink those for 30–90%. This plugin bolts that filtering onto `dsh`'s bash execu
tor so every eligible command is auto-routed through `rtk` — **with zero semantic change** to what a
eligible command is auto-routed through `rtk` — **with zero semantic change** to what actually runs.
## How it works
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Two guards decide (see `src/wrap.ts` and `src/rtk.ts`):
1. **The mapping is rtk's, not ours.** `resolve()` spawns `rtk rewrite <command>` and adopts whateve
r it prints on stdout. The plugin keeps no table of commands: when rtk ships a new rule, upgrading r
tk upgrades the plugin's coverage, and the plugin does not need a release. The exit code is ignored
on purpose — rtk uses it for its own Claude Code permission protocol, which has no counterpart here.
2. **A cheap cost filter, not a policy.** The command is split on top-level control operators (`&&`
, `||`, `;`, `|`, `|&`, `&`, newline) and each segment's first word is checked: shell keywords and e
veryday builtins (`cd`, `echo`, `export`, …) do not make a segment routable on their own. A command
is skipped only when **every** segment is such a builtin — `cd repo && cargo test` is handed to rtk,
and comes back as `cd repo && rtk cargo test`. Anything not provably unroutable is handed to rtk to
decide. If the `rtk` binary is absent the whole transform is the **identity**, so the deployment be
haves exactly like the stock executor.
Commands are *lexed* by rtk, not matched as whole strings: it rewrites the segments it recognizes an
d preserves pipes, `&&`/`;`, redirections and substitutions byte-for-byte. Compound commands are the
refore routed, not skipped.
### Versioning note
The plugin **does not bundle or pin rtk**. At executor construction it probes `rtk --version` on `PA
TH` (see `probeRtkAvailable` in `src/rtk.ts`) and then asks that same binary to do the rewriting. Th
`probeRtkAvailable` in `src/rtk.ts`) and then asks that same binary to do the rewriting. Therefore:
- When **rtk ships a new release**, any user who upgrades `rtk` on their machine automatically gets

the new rules *and the new commands* — no plugin update required.
- The plugin version (this repo) a
nd the rtk version are **independent**; keep them separate. This README states the *minimum* rtk ver

sion tested against, not a lockstep number.
[该节后续省略]
### Compatibility & version alignment
This plugin depends on `@deepseek-ai/dsh-*` packages that DeepSeek Harness publishes to npm **indepe
ndently** from the `dsh` aggregate package. Those sub-packages (and `dsh` itself) ship as **prerelea
ses** (`x.y.z-rc.n`). Under plain node-semver a prerelease only satisfies a range when some comparat
or shares its exact `major.minor.patch` tuple *and* carries a prerelease tag — which is why the uppe
r bound is written `<0.3.0-0` rather than `<0.3.0`. The runtime loader is more permissive than that:
`dsh-app-boot` evaluates `engines.dsh` and the plugin's dsh peer ranges with `includePrerelease: tr
ue`, so these peer ranges match every `0.1.x`/`0.2.x` prerelease. Peer ranges are advisory, though:
the `engines.dsh` gate documented below is what actually decides whether the bundle loads.

e container at runtime, but it injects the **scoped** `@deepseek-ai/cordis`, which is the package th
is plugin imports for its `Context`/`Service` types. The unscoped npm name `cordis` is a *different,
older* line (`4.0.0-rc.11`) and must not be used here.
